## Motivation

Starting an engine with `prefill_max_requests=0` completes model setup, then the first `generate()` call blocks. Current `main` still accepts the value and passes it to the scheduler, where the first request fails the admission check because `0 >= 0`.

Fail during argument resolution, before model startup. Fixes https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23788.

## Modifications

Reject non-positive `prefill_max_requests` values in the model-independent `ServerArgs` validation path. The parameterized CPU test covers `0` and `-1`. Valid positive values and the default `None` keep their existing behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable. This only validates configuration.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. Valid configurations use the same scheduler path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on both changed files.
- [x] Add unit tests. See the raw test output below.
- Documentation: not needed. The existing help already describes `None` as no limit.
- Accuracy and speed benchmarks: not applicable.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style. The repository's touched-file pre-commit subset passed.

<details>
<summary>Red and green logs</summary>

The linked issue records the live GPU repro: `generate()` did not return within 60 seconds. On current `upstream/main`, the model-independent argument path still accepted the invalid value:

```text
$ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs
args = ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=0)
args.resolve_once()
print(f"resolution=accepted value={args.prefill_max_requests}")
PY
resolution=accepted value=0
```

After the fix:

```text
$ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py TestPrepareServerArgs
Ran 6 tests in 0.053s
OK

$ TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -c 'from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs; ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=0).resolve_once()'
ValueError: --prefill-max-requests must be positive when set.
```

</details>

Thanks @1fanwang. Closing this because you have 6 PRs open and none updated in 7 days, over our soft cap of 5 for idle PRs.

Reopen the two or three you most want reviewed - a short active set moves faster than a long idle one.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

Hi @1fanwang, thanks for this fix. `--prefill-max-requests 0` is still accepted on main: the admission check in `schedule_policy.py` (`len(self.can_run_list) >= x`) is true on the first request for `x == 0`, so nothing is ever admitted (#23788, which the stale bot closed in June without a fix). #23826 was closed by the bot on Oct 24 and now conflicts after #44001.

I've carried your check onto current main with a test, and it passes. I'll open it as a PR in three days unless you'd rather reopen yours; if you want to, say so and I'll hold off. You're credited as co-author on the commit.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a validation check for `prefill_max_requests` in `ServerArgs` to ensure it is either `None` or a positive integer, preventing potential scheduler deadlocks. It also adds unit tests to verify this behavior. Feedback suggests explicitly setting `served_model_name` in the new test cases to avoid a potential `TypeError` during the validation process, ensuring the tests are more robust.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `ServerArgs` instantiation with `model_path="dummy"` causes `__post_init__` to return early (line 782 in `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`), which leaves `served_model_name` as `None`. When `check_server_args()` is called, it will likely raise a `TypeError` at line 6657 when attempting to check `":" not in self.served_model_name`. 

To ensure these tests are robust and don't fail due to this pre-existing issue in `check_server_args`, consider explicitly setting `served_model_name="dummy"` in the test cases. This applies to lines 179, 186, and 192 as well.

```suggestion
        server_args = ServerArgs(model_path="dummy", prefill_max_requests=None, served_model_name="dummy")
```
